messages:
sam: Quick heads-up — ran a targeted microprofile on ga-prod yesterday after the 11:10 alert. 429 spikes correlate tightly with a prefetched-KV gap that appears when we swap kernels for long-context (>1024) requests.
anya: timeline + logs? can you paste the profiler output or a short summary?
sam: summary below — short snip from the run (11:12–11:22):
```
prefetch_hit_rate: 0.72 -> 0.38
prefetch_miss_ratio: 0.28 -> 0.62
batch_size_avg: 12
avg_latency_ms: 240
kernel_swap_events: 7  (each ~100ms pause)
429_rate: 0 -> 18/min spike window
```
mike: hm, so when kernel swap happens we pause prefetch / KV warmup and new requests miss the cache and therefore blow token budgets?
sam: that's the hypothesis. kernel swap triggers a short period where the prefetched KV lanes are cold and batch assembly aggressively coalesces requests -> larger token budgets and more throughput pressure. lots of soft rejects cascade into 429s.
nora: suggestion: introduce a small "swap grace" window that delays admission changes for the slab being swapped, and bias fallthrough to pools that have recent prefetch hits. e.g., `swap_grace_ms=150` + `prefetch_fallthrough_bias=0.8`. gives the KV layer time to warm without stalling overall throughput.
anya: can you simulate that setup in canary? maybe run 4-hour litmus with traffic replay. also add a metric for prefetch-gap and a kernel_swap_event counter so dashboards can correlate.
sam: ran a quick A/B 30m canary with `prefetch_fallthrough_bias=0.8` and `swap_grace_ms=150`. Results (canary vs baseline): 429s down ~73%, p99 latency down 8%, CPU +3%. uploaded charts: https://grafana.internal/rdw/d/kv-prefetch/overview (internal)
perf-bot: perf-test summary: canary: stable; cpu_regression: +3.1%; p99_latency_delta: -8.2%; kv_hit_delta: +19.0%; 429_count_delta: -72.6%. Test ID: perf-2026-03-16-11
mike: promising tradeoff. plan: 1) feature flag these params behind FF, 2) 24h canary on ga-prod region, 3) add prefetch-gap histogram + kernel_swap_event annotation on dashboards, 4) short postmortem playbook entry for 429 waves.
sam: created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 — adds `swap_grace_ms`, `prefetch_fallthrough_bias`, and emits `prefetch_gap_hist` + `kernel_swap_event` tags. includes unit tests for admission gating.
anya: I'll run the 24h canary tomorrow morning and review perf logs. merging contingent on no silent regressions in tail latency. cc @mike
nora: also adding a short doc to eng-runtime playbook on investigating 429 waves and how to toggle the bias flag for emergency mitigation.
mike: I'll draft the playbook bullet points and link to the PR. we should include sample queries: `sum(rate(prefetch_miss[5m])) by (region)` and `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le)(prefetch_gap_hist))`.
sam: thanks all — moving this into the retro for next eng-runtime sync.
